name: Grammarly

Software Engineer.dsaDepth: Heavy - LeetCode-medium-to-hard problems delivered as much through open discussion of trade-offs as through pure correctness, in a long, structured 5-round loop
rounds: Recruiter call (~30 min): motivation, role fit, logistics - Grammarly is explicit about remote-first expectations and relocation up front
Coding screen (~1 hr): LeetCode-medium algorithmic problems under time pressure
System design round: distributed systems and architecture trade-offs at scale
Onsite coding round (part of a ~5.5 hr onsite): LeetCode-hard, debugging, code clarity and edge cases (a rate limiter and a graph-deep-copy-on-a-whiteboard are both reported)
Project-impact / experience round: walking through a major past project and justifying design choices, with emphasis on real product impact, not just technical correctness
Manager and/or culture-values round (Grammarly’s "EAGER" values framework)
extraTopics: Explaining trade-offs and complexity out loud, even more than reaching a fast answer - several candidates note the interviewers listen for clarity and structure over memorized patterns
Connecting technical decisions to real product impact - a recurring, explicitly product-minded evaluation lens
A referral reportedly guarantees a callback here, more reliably than at many other companies
Software Engineer.notes: Reported pass rate is around 33-45% in the US pipeline (Taro-aggregated data) - a genuinely selective loop, not a formality.
